functions.name: Observations
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(Y, [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    ROWS(FILTER(Y, filt_arg))
  ))

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: n — count of rows used in the regression as a scalar integer
functions.description:
n (number of observations) is the count of data points available to the model after any filtering is applied. It is the fundamental sample size that drives all degrees-of-freedom calculations.

Returns ROWS(FILTER(Y, filt_arg)). X_s is not required because row count is fully determined by Y.

functions.name: DF_Regression
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s,
  COLUMNS(X_s))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

functions.yields: df_regression (k, number of predictors) as a scalar integer
functions.description:
df_regression is the number of degrees of freedom attributable to the regression model — equal to k, the number of predictor columns. The intercept term (if any) is not counted here; it is accounted for implicitly in df_total.

Returns COLUMNS(X_s). Filter and Allow_Intercept do not affect this value.

functions.name: DF_Total
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    n,         Observations(Y, filt_arg),
    IF(allow_arg, n - 1, n)
  ))

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: df_total (n-1 with intercept, n without) as a scalar integer
functions.description:
df_total is the total degrees of freedom for the sum of squares. When an intercept is fit (default), one df is spent estimating the grand mean, giving n - 1. When the model is forced through the origin (Allow_Intercept = FALSE), no df is spent on the mean, giving n. df_total partitions into df_regression + df_residual.

Calls Observations() for n, then returns IF(allow_arg, n-1, n).

functions.name: R_squared
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    INDEX(LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE), 3, 1)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: R² (coefficient of determination) as a scalar in [0, 1]
functions.description:
R² (coefficient of determination) is the proportion of variance in Y explained by the regression model. It equals SS_regression / SS_total, ranges from 0 (no explanatory power) to 1 (perfect fit), and is the square of Multiple R.

Returns INDEX(LINEST(...), 3, 1) directly. R_squared is the base statistic from which Multiple_R and Adjusted_R2 are derived.

functions.name: DF_Residual
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    DF_Total(Y, allow_arg, filt_arg) - DF_Regression(X_s)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: df_residual (n-k-1 with intercept, n-k without) as a scalar integer
functions.description:
df_residual (also called df_error) is the degrees of freedom remaining after the regression model has been fit. With an intercept it equals n - k - 1; without an intercept it equals n - k. It is the denominator degrees of freedom for the F-test and the penalty term in Adjusted R².

Computed as DF_Total(...) - DF_Regression(...), inheriting the Allow_Intercept correction from DF_Total.

functions.name: Multiple_R
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    SQRT(R_squared(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: Multiple R (correlation coefficient) as a scalar in [0, 1]
functions.description:
Multiple R is the Pearson correlation between the observed values of Y and the values predicted by the regression model. It ranges from 0 (no linear relationship) to 1 (perfect linear fit) and is the square root of R².

Computed as SQRT(R_squared(...)).

functions.name: Adjusted_R2
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    1 - (1 - R_squared(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg))
      * DF_Total(Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
      / DF_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: Adjusted R² as a scalar, typically in [0, 1] but can be negative
functions.description:
Adjusted R² penalises R² for the number of predictors relative to sample size, correcting for the inflation that occurs when irrelevant predictors are added. It equals 1 - (1 - R²) × df_total / df_residual, which reduces to the familiar 1 - (1 - R²)(n-1)/(n-k-1) when an intercept is fit. Unlike R² it can decrease when a predictor adds less explanatory power than expected by chance, and can be negative when the model fits worse than a horizontal line.

Computed as 1 - (1 - R_squared(...)) * DF_Total(...) / DF_Residual(...), inheriting the Allow_Intercept correction from both df functions.

functions.name: SS_Residual
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    INDEX(LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE), 5, 2)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SS_residual (error sum of squares) as a scalar
functions.description:
SS_residual (also written SSE or SS_error) is the sum of squared differences between each observed Y value and its model-fitted value: Σ(yᵢ - ŷᵢ)². It measures the variance left unexplained by the regression and is the numerator of MSE = SS_residual / df_residual. Together with SS_regression it partitions SS_total.

Returns INDEX(LINEST(..., TRUE), 5, 2). Position (5, 2) of the LINEST stats array is SS_residual; position (5, 1) is SS_regression.

functions.name: SS_Total
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    Y_f, FILTER(Y, filt_arg),
    IF(allow_arg, DEVSQ(Y_f), SUMSQ(Y_f))
  ))

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SS_total as a scalar
functions.description:
SS_total is the total variability in Y before any regression model is applied. When an intercept is fit (default) it equals DEVSQ(Y) = Σ(yᵢ - ȳ)², the sum of squared deviations from the mean. When the model is forced through the origin it equals SUMSQ(Y) = Σyᵢ², because there is no mean to subtract. SS_total = SS_regression + SS_residual in both cases.

X_s is not required because SS_total depends only on Y and whether an intercept is included. Uses DEVSQ for the intercept case and SUMSQ for the no-intercept case.

functions.name: SS_Regression
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    INDEX(LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE), 5, 1)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SS_regression (explained sum of squares) as a scalar
functions.description:
SS_regression (also written SSR or SS_model) is the portion of total variability in Y that is explained by the regression model: Σ(ŷᵢ - ȳ)². It equals SS_total - SS_residual and is the numerator of the F-statistic (F = (SS_regression / df_regression) / MSE). R² = SS_regression / SS_total.

Returns INDEX(LINEST(..., TRUE), 5, 1). Position (5, 1) of the LINEST stats array is SS_regression; position (5, 2) is SS_residual.

functions.name: SE_Regression
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    INDEX(LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE), 3, 2)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SE_regression (root mean square error, RMSE) as a scalar
functions.description:
SE_regression is the standard error of the regression, also called the root mean square error (RMSE) or s. It equals √(SS_residual / df_residual) = √MSE and is measured in the same units as Y. It estimates the standard deviation of the residuals and is used as the base uncertainty in prediction intervals.

Returns INDEX(LINEST(..., TRUE), 3, 2). Position (3, 2) of the LINEST stats array holds the standard error of the regression; position (3, 1) is R².

functions.name: Coefficients
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    ls,     LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,      COLUMNS(X_s),
    n_coef, IF(allow_arg, k + 1, k),
    _xlfn.MAKEARRAY(n_coef, 1, LAMBDA(r, c, INDEX(ls, 1, n_coef + 1 - r)))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: (k+1)×1 spill with intercept first, then b₁…bₖ — or k×1 when Allow_Intercept is FALSE
functions.description:
Coefficients returns the fitted regression coefficients as a vertical array in natural order: intercept (b₀) first when an intercept is included, followed by the slope for the first predictor column through the last (b₁, b₂, …, bₖ).

LINEST stores coefficients in reverse order (bₖ first, b₀ last). MAKEARRAY reverses this by reading column n_coef+1−r at each row r, producing the Analysis ToolPak ordering. This function spills and must be entered in a blank column range of at least k+1 rows.

functions.name: Standard_Errors
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    ls,     LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,      COLUMNS(X_s),
    n_coef, IF(allow_arg, k + 1, k),
    MAKEARRAY(n_coef, 1, LAMBDA(r, c, INDEX(ls, 2, n_coef + 1 - r)))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: (k+1)×1 spill of coefficient standard errors, intercept first — or k×1 when Allow_Intercept is FALSE
functions.description:
Standard_Errors returns the standard error of each fitted coefficient in the same natural order as Coefficients: SE(b₀) first (when an intercept is fit), then SE(b₁) through SE(bₖ). Each SE measures sampling uncertainty in the corresponding coefficient; dividing the coefficient by its SE yields the t-statistic.

Uses LINEST row 2, reversed via the same MAKEARRAY pattern as Coefficients. The result is parallel to Coefficients — row i of Standard_Errors corresponds to row i of Coefficients.

functions.name: T_Stats
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    ls,     LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,      COLUMNS(X_s),
    n_coef, IF(allow_arg, k + 1, k),
    MAKEARRAY(n_coef, 1, LAMBDA(r, c,
      INDEX(ls, 1, n_coef + 1 - r) / INDEX(ls, 2, n_coef + 1 - r)
    ))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: (k+1)×1 spill of t-statistics, intercept first — or k×1 when Allow_Intercept is FALSE
functions.description:
T_Stats returns the t-statistic for each coefficient, defined as bⱼ / SE(bⱼ). Under H₀: bⱼ = 0 the statistic follows a t-distribution with df_residual degrees of freedom. Large absolute values indicate that the coefficient is unlikely to be zero by chance.

Divides LINEST row 1 by row 2 element-wise inside MAKEARRAY, using the same reversal as Coefficients so the output is in natural order (intercept first). The reference distribution for inference is T with df_residual = INDEX(LINEST(...), 4, 2) degrees of freedom.

functions.name: P_Values
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    ls,     LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,      COLUMNS(X_s),
    df_r,   INDEX(ls, 4, 2),
    n_coef, IF(allow_arg, k + 1, k),
    MAKEARRAY(n_coef, 1, LAMBDA(r, c,
      T.DIST.2T(
        ABS(INDEX(ls, 1, n_coef + 1 - r) / INDEX(ls, 2, n_coef + 1 - r)),
        df_r
      )
    ))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: (k+1)×1 spill of two-tailed p-values, intercept first — or k×1 when Allow_Intercept is FALSE
functions.description:
P_Values returns the two-tailed p-value for the null hypothesis H₀: bⱼ = 0 for each coefficient. P_value = T.DIST.2T(|tⱼ|, df_residual). Values below a chosen α (typically 0.05) indicate the coefficient is statistically significant at that level.

Computed inside MAKEARRAY so all p-values share the single LINEST call. The df_residual used is INDEX(ls, 4, 2), which is the value Excel already computed internally. Output is in natural order (intercept first), parallel to Coefficients, Standard_Errors, and T_Stats.

functions.name: CI_Lower
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter], [Confidence_Level],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept),  TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),           TRUE, Filter),
    conf,      IF(ISOMITTED(Confidence_Level), 0.95, Confidence_Level),
    ls,     LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,      COLUMNS(X_s),
    df_r,   INDEX(ls, 4, 2),
    t_crit, T.INV.2T(1 - conf, df_r),
    n_coef, IF(allow_arg, k + 1, k),
    MAKEARRAY(n_coef, 1, LAMBDA(r, c,
      INDEX(ls, 1, n_coef + 1 - r) - t_crit * INDEX(ls, 2, n_coef + 1 - r)
    ))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

arguments.name: Confidence_Level
arguments.description: confidence level as a decimal, e.g. 0.95 for 95%. Default 0.95

functions.yields: (k+1)×1 spill of lower confidence-interval bounds, intercept first — or k×1 when Allow_Intercept is FALSE
functions.description:
CI_Lower returns the lower bound of the confidence interval for each coefficient: bⱼ − t* × SE(bⱼ), where t* = T.INV.2T(1 − confidence_level, df_residual). With the default confidence_level of 0.95 this produces 95% lower bounds, matching the Analysis ToolPak output.

Output is in natural order (intercept first), parallel to Coefficients. Use CI_Excludes_Zero to test significance: a lower bound above zero, or an upper bound below zero, implies the coefficient is significantly different from zero at the chosen confidence level.

functions.name: CI_Upper
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter], [Confidence_Level],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept),  TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),           TRUE, Filter),
    conf,      IF(ISOMITTED(Confidence_Level), 0.95, Confidence_Level),
    ls,     LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,      COLUMNS(X_s),
    df_r,   INDEX(ls, 4, 2),
    t_crit, T.INV.2T(1 - conf, df_r),
    n_coef, IF(allow_arg, k + 1, k),
    MAKEARRAY(n_coef, 1, LAMBDA(r, c,
      INDEX(ls, 1, n_coef + 1 - r) + t_crit * INDEX(ls, 2, n_coef + 1 - r)
    ))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

arguments.name: Confidence_Level
arguments.description: confidence level as a decimal, e.g. 0.95 for 95%. Default 0.95

functions.yields: (k+1)×1 spill of upper confidence-interval bounds, intercept first — or k×1 when Allow_Intercept is FALSE
functions.description:
CI_Upper returns the upper bound of the confidence interval for each coefficient: bⱼ + t* × SE(bⱼ), where t* = T.INV.2T(1 − confidence_level, df_residual). With the default confidence_level of 0.95 this produces 95% upper bounds, matching the Analysis ToolPak output.

Mirrors CI_Lower exactly, with addition instead of subtraction. Output is in natural order (intercept first). The pair (CI_Lower, CI_Upper) brackets the plausible range for each coefficient at the chosen confidence level.

functions.name: CI_Excludes_Zero
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter], [Confidence_Level],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept),  TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),           TRUE, Filter),
    conf,      IF(ISOMITTED(Confidence_Level), 0.95, Confidence_Level),
    ls,     LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,      COLUMNS(X_s),
    df_r,   INDEX(ls, 4, 2),
    t_crit, T.INV.2T(1 - conf, df_r),
    n_coef, IF(allow_arg, k + 1, k),
    MAKEARRAY(n_coef, 1, LAMBDA(r, c,
      LET(
        coef,  INDEX(ls, 1, n_coef + 1 - r),
        se,    INDEX(ls, 2, n_coef + 1 - r),
        lower, coef - t_crit * se,
        upper, coef + t_crit * se,
        OR(lower > 0, upper < 0)
      )
    ))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

arguments.name: Confidence_Level
arguments.description: confidence level as a decimal, e.g. 0.95 for 95%. Default 0.95

functions.yields: (k+1)×1 spill of TRUE/FALSE — TRUE means the CI excludes zero (coefficient is significant)
functions.description:
CI_Excludes_Zero returns TRUE for each coefficient whose confidence interval does not contain zero, indicating statistical significance at the chosen confidence level. A coefficient is significant when CI_Lower > 0 (positive effect) or CI_Upper < 0 (negative effect).

Equivalent to testing P_Values < (1 − confidence_level), but expressed in terms of the CI bounds for use in conditional formatting or logical formulas. Computed by OR(lower > 0, upper < 0) inside MAKEARRAY, reusing the same LINEST call for all coefficients.

functions.name: Fitted_Values
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    X_f,   FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    Y_f,   FILTER(Y,   filt_arg),
    ls,    LINEST(Y_f, X_f, allow_arg, TRUE),
    k,     COLUMNS(X_s),
    betas, MAKEARRAY(k, 1, LAMBDA(r, c, INDEX(ls, 1, k + 1 - r))),
    b0,    IF(allow_arg, INDEX(ls, 1, k + 1), 0),
    MMULT(X_f, betas) + b0
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: n×1 spill of fitted (predicted) values ŷᵢ
functions.description:
Fitted_Values returns the model-predicted value ŷᵢ = b₀ + b₁x₁ᵢ + ⋯ + bₖxₖᵢ for each observation in the filtered training data. The result is parallel to the filtered Y column — row i corresponds to the i-th included observation.

Extracts the k predictor coefficients [b₁, …, bₖ] from LINEST row 1 in natural order using MAKEARRAY, then computes MMULT(X_f, betas) + b0. When Allow_Intercept is FALSE, b0 = 0. Fitted_Values is the base for Residuals, and indirectly for LOOCV_Predicted.

functions.name: Residuals
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    FILTER(Y, filt_arg) - Fitted_Values(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
  ))

arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

functions.yields: n×1 spill of ordinary residuals eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ
functions.description:
Residuals returns the ordinary (raw) residual eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ for each observation in the filtered training data. Residuals should average to zero when an intercept is fit, be free of patterns when plotted against fitted values (homoscedasticity), and be approximately normal for inference to be valid.

Computed as FILTER(Y, filt_arg) − Fitted_Values(...). Residuals are the input to LOOCV_Residuals and are used alongside Leverage to compute the PRESS statistic.

functions.name: Leverage
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    X_f,     FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    n,       ROWS(FILTER(Y, filt_arg)),
    X_aug,   IF(allow_arg, HSTACK(SEQUENCE(n, 1, 1, 0), X_f), X_f),
    XtX_inv, MINVERSE(MMULT(TRANSPOSE(X_aug), X_aug)),
    BYROW(X_aug, LAMBDA(row, MMULT(MMULT(row, XtX_inv), TRANSPOSE(row))))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range — used only to determine n after filtering

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: n×1 spill of hat-matrix diagonal values hᵢᵢ ∈ [0, 1]
functions.description:
Leverage returns the diagonal of the hat matrix H = X_aug(X_augᵀX_aug)⁻¹X_augᵀ, where X_aug prepends a column of ones when an intercept is fit. The value hᵢᵢ measures how far observation i lies from the centroid of the predictor space; high leverage (hᵢᵢ > 2p/n, where p is the number of parameters) flags observations with unusual predictor patterns that have disproportionate influence on the fitted line. hᵢᵢ lies in [0, 1]: the lower bound of 0 can occur when Allow_Intercept is FALSE and all predictor values for that row are zero; the upper bound of 1 is reached only when n equals the number of fitted parameters.

BYROW computes xᵢᵀ(XᵀX)⁻¹xᵢ for each row using a single MINVERSE call. SEQUENCE(n, 1, 1, 0) builds the intercept column of ones. Leverage values are the denominators in the Sherman-Morrison LOO shortcut used by LOOCV_Residuals.

functions.name: LOOCV_Residuals
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    e, Residuals(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    h, Leverage(X_s,  Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    e / (1 - h)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: n×1 spill of leave-one-out cross-validated residuals ê₍₋ᵢ₎ = eᵢ / (1 − hᵢᵢ)
functions.description:
LOOCV_Residuals returns the deleted residual for each observation: the difference between yᵢ and the value that would have been predicted by a model trained on all n − 1 other observations. Computing n separate regressions is avoided via the Sherman-Morrison identity ê₍₋ᵢ₎ = eᵢ / (1 − hᵢᵢ), which requires only the ordinary residual and the leverage value from the full-data fit.

Calls Residuals() and Leverage() and divides elementwise. For nonzero residuals, LOOCV residuals are larger in magnitude than ordinary residuals whenever hᵢᵢ > 0; when eᵢ = 0 the LOOCV residual is also 0 regardless of leverage. LOOCV residuals are the inputs to PRESS. An observation with high leverage and a large LOOCV residual is both unusual and poorly predicted.

functions.name: LOOCV_Predicted
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],

    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    Y_f, FILTER(Y, filt_arg),
    Y_f - LOOCV_Residuals(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
  ))

functions.yields: n×1 spill of leave-one-out cross-validated predictions ŷ₍₋ᵢ₎
functions.description:
LOOCV_Predicted returns the prediction each observation would have received from a model trained on all other observations. It equals yᵢ − ê₍₋ᵢ₎ = yᵢ − eᵢ/(1 − hᵢᵢ), derived from the Sherman-Morrison shortcut without refitting the model n times.

Computed as FILTER(Y, filt_arg) − LOOCV_Residuals(...). Plotting LOOCV_Predicted vs Y gives a cross-validated fit diagnostic; the R² of this plot is a more honest estimate of predictive accuracy than the in-sample R².

functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),

functions.yields: PRESS statistic as a scalar — sum of squared LOO residuals
functions.description:
PRESS (Predicted Residual Error Sum of Squares) is the sum of squared leave-one-out cross-validated residuals: Σ[eᵢ/(1 − hᵢᵢ)]². It measures out-of-sample predictive accuracy on the same scale as SS_residual; lower PRESS indicates a model that generalises better. PRESS ≥ SS_residual; equality holds when all residuals are zero (perfect fit) or when hᵢᵢ = 0 for every observation with a nonzero residual.

Computed as SUMSQ(LOOCV_Residuals(...)). PRESS is a scalar summary of the LOOCV_Residuals array and belongs in the model summary table alongside SS_residual, SE_regression, and R².

functions.name: Prediction_Interval
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, X_new, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter], [Confidence_Level],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept),  TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),           TRUE, Filter),
    conf,      IF(ISOMITTED(Confidence_Level), 0.95, Confidence_Level),
    X_f,   FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    Y_f,   FILTER(Y,   filt_arg),
    n,     ROWS(Y_f),
    k,     COLUMNS(X_s),
    ls,    LINEST(Y_f, X_f, allow_arg, TRUE),
    df_r,  INDEX(ls, 4, 2),
    se_r,  INDEX(ls, 3, 2),
    betas, MAKEARRAY(k, 1, LAMBDA(r, c, INDEX(ls, 1, k + 1 - r))),
    b0,    IF(allow_arg, INDEX(ls, 1, k + 1), 0),
    X_new_row, IF(ROWS(X_new) = 1, X_new, TRANSPOSE(X_new)),
    y_hat_new, MMULT(X_new_row, betas) + b0,
    X_aug,    IF(allow_arg, HSTACK(SEQUENCE(n, 1, 1, 0), X_f), X_f),
    XtX_inv,  MINVERSE(MMULT(TRANSPOSE(X_aug), X_aug)),
    X_new_aug, IF(allow_arg, HSTACK(1, X_new_row), X_new_row),
    h_new,    MMULT(MMULT(X_new_aug, XtX_inv), TRANSPOSE(X_new_aug)),
    se_pred,  se_r * SQRT(1 + h_new),
    t_crit,   T.INV.2T(1 - conf, df_r),
    VSTACK(
      y_hat_new,
      se_pred,
      t_crit,
      y_hat_new - t_crit * se_pred,
      y_hat_new + t_crit * se_pred,
      conf
    )
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column) — the training data

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range — the training data

arguments.name: X_new
arguments.description: 1×k row (or k×1 column) of predictor values for the new observation, e.g. a row reference from tbl_Prediction_Inputs

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

arguments.name: Confidence_Level
arguments.description: confidence level as a decimal, e.g. 0.95 for 95%. Default 0.95

functions.yields: 6×1 spill: Point_Estimate, SE_Prediction, T_Critical, Lower_Bound, Upper_Bound, Confidence_Level
functions.description:
Prediction_Interval returns a 6-row vertical spill containing everything needed to report a prediction for a new observation: (1) the point estimate ŷ_new = b₀ + b₁x₁ + ⋯ + bₖxₖ; (2) the standard error of prediction SE_pred = s√(1 + x_newᵀ(XᵀX)⁻¹x_new); (3) the t-critical value t* = T.INV.2T(1 − conf, df_residual); (4) the lower bound ŷ_new − t*·SE_pred; (5) the upper bound ŷ_new + t*·SE_pred; (6) the confidence level used.

The prediction interval is wider than a confidence interval for the mean response because it includes an extra factor of 1 inside the square root, accounting for the irreducible residual variance of a single new observation. X_new must have exactly k columns matching X_s; both 1×k and k×1 orientations are accepted via the ROWS(X_new) = 1 check. Typically entered in a column aligned with a row from tbl_Prediction_Inputs.
